test_title: PYST 11: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following best defines the strategy of Passive Resistance as advocated by Extremists?

options.text: Boycott, Swadeshi and non-cooperation with rulers
Military training of Indian youth abroad

solution:
The correct answer is __**Boycott, Swadeshi and non-cooperation with rulers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive Resistance** was a strategy promoted by the **Extremists** during the **Indian freedom struggle**. It involved non-violent and peaceful methods to oppose British colonial rule.
 
• The **Extremists**, led by leaders like **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**, emphasized self-reliance and the use of indigenous methods to resist foreign rule.
 
• **Boycott Movement:** The Extremists urged Indians to boycott British goods, schools, and services to cripple the colonial economy and administration. This was a peaceful and non-violent way of opposing British policies.
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:** They promoted the use of **Swadeshi goods** (Indian-made products) and advocated for the establishment of indigenous industries to reduce dependence on British imports.
 
• **Non-Cooperation:** The Extremists encouraged Indians to refuse cooperation with British authorities, including boycotting institutions, resigning from government jobs, and refusing to pay taxes. This was a key component of passive resistance.
 
• The Extremists focused on building national consciousness and self-respect, urging Indians to embrace their identity and reject British domination. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Other options, such as **assassination of British officers**, **military training abroad**, or **armed confrontation**, do not align with the principles of Passive Resistance and were not advocated by the Extremists. These statements are incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Boycott Movement:**

 
 
• The **Boycott Movement** was one of the earliest forms of protest against British goods and institutions. It was initiated during the **Swadeshi Movement** (1905–1908) after the **Partition of Bengal**.
 
• The strategy aimed to reduce the economic benefits that the British derived from India and encourage Indians to support indigenous industries.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• The **Swadeshi Movement** was a part of Passive Resistance and focused on promoting Indian goods, industries, and self-reliance.
 
• This movement inspired the establishment of **Indian textile mills, banks, and educational institutions** to counter British imports and services.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation:**
 
 
• **Non-cooperation** was a peaceful method of resistance where Indians were encouraged to **withdraw from British institutions, reject British titles and honors**, and refuse to pay taxes.
 
 
 
• **Key Leaders of the Extremist Movement:**
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** Known as the "Father of Indian Unrest," Tilak promoted Swaraj (self-rule) and used the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it."
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal:** A strong proponent of Swadeshi and Boycott, he emphasized self-reliance and the need for national awakening.
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:** Known as the "Lion of Punjab," he advocated for self-rule and encouraged Indians to embrace their cultural heritage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Concepts of Passive Resistance:**

 
 
• **Non-violence:** Passive Resistance was inherently non-violent and aimed at achieving political and social goals through peaceful methods.
 
• **Self-reliance:** The movement sought to empower Indians by promoting indigenous industries, education, and self-governance.
 
 
 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**
 
 
• The Partition of Bengal was a major event that sparked the Swadeshi and Boycott Movements. It was seen as an attempt by the British to divide Indians along communal lines.
 
• The Partition was eventually annulled in **1911**, demonstrating the effectiveness of Passive Resistance.
